newsitem.title: CANADA: BMO's Nesbitt Burns denies hurt by Bre-X.
newsitem.headline: BMO's Nesbitt Burns denies hurt by Bre-X.

text.p: Canadian brokerage firm Nesbitt Burns, a wholly owned unit of Bank of Montreal, denied market rumors on Thursday that it had been especially hurt by the Bre-X Minerals Ltd debacle.
"That's absolutely untrue," said Nesbitt Burns Deputy Chairman and Chief Operating Officer Aubrey Baillie.
"There is no significant financial impact on Nesbitt Burns or the Bank of Montreal as a result of the change in the share price of Bre-X," Baillie added.
Bailey said Nesbitt has only "nominal positions" of Bre-X stock in the brokerage's own accounts.
A source close to the brokerage said Nesbitt had a long position of less than C$100 million of Bre-X.
Market rumor had pegged Nesbitt with a C$500 million long position in the Calgary-based miner.
Bailey said Nesbitt Burns was simply "one of a number of underwriters, (and) probably one of the most active traders in the stock."
Bank of Montreal spokesman Joe Barbera said the bank is in the same position as other Canadian institutional investors who had dealt in Bre-X.
"We're in the same position as everyone else, in a wait-and-see position on results of the different analysis of the ore that's been going on and we're going to stay tuned."
